title: Yes, I Use AI to Make My Game | A Solo Dev Responds to the Hate
author: JustAGirlInSpace2

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: Approving this post. This got flagged for essentially \_only\_ complaining about Anti AI sentiment, which we're cracking down on. However the long form format of youtube videos allows more nuanced discussions and a quick review of the video I see it talks process.

comments.author: JustAGirlInSpace2

comments.body: no one here makes games any more, now we are making videos about ai hate,.... make good games and this would all go away, keep producing low quality games it gives them ammo to throw back at you

replies.author: Tkwan777
replies.body: Even with AI assistance, its going to take a year or more for the good ones to come out. Pro studios could probably pop out large games in roughly year also since they have large teams that can all use ai in their various departments.

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: yet people still put out very low quality rushed items. usually the honest ones admit the pushed it too much,  I'm just saying take time do the best you can. Consistency isn't that hard to do but  when you just go "Ai make me game" then "Ai add this feature" its not going to work unless you go back and test and actually play and review your game looking for problems.  Lots of  people are still too impressed on what AI can do and don't take time to smooth out rough edges, and get offended when people point them out. I'm as far as anti ai as you can get, but a good portion of the ones Is ee are poor and its not the models fault

comments.author: mrpoopistan
comments.body:
Worth remembering that Chinese bot farms fan AI hate to hold back US development.

Except for the most "bro, did you even try stuff," I see very little direct hatred for AI-assisted games when I venture into other subs. For example, I can see the hallmarks of AI in a decent amount of the games that people promote on r/sciencefiction, and none of those threads erupt with AI hatred.

The most grassroots hatred tends to come from creative subs, and a lot of those are justified by the general badness of AI for those tasks, such as drawing and writing.

comments.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
comments.body: Just tell them that, friend! I agree with you!

comments.author: CoolTIOnline
comments.body:
I started building my first game on a whim, which was something I always wanted to do and as I started using Godot and Claude's help, I have gone so far and built something so fun that I can't wait to release... only in the last month or so I came to reddit to advertise in different groups and holy crap did I see how much the use of AI is hated on certain groups. I get it, I understand the issues that come with the use of AI.  
However AI is a tool and it enables people who have vision and who wish to realize their dream, their passion and put in serious work into it... they can make something awesome and at that point, that person is a Game Dev and an Artist as he has realized his vision.

comments.author: D3c1m470r
comments.body:
Thanks for putting this out there.   
I hope it gets watched by all those haters who probably never going to understand that being a solo-dev is just so incredibly involving and would be impossible for most of us without these tools.  
I usually use the metaphor - are you also hating on mathematicians for using a calculator instead of hand-writing everything?

comments.author: Special_Eye4266
comments.body:
Ai IS a tool, not an automatic slop machine. Just like any other practice, an artist could take a paint brush and fling paint at it randomly or they can use their brush with precision and care to create the detail that their imagination desires. People are so caught up on capabilities that they rush before understanding the tool itself. Can you imagine if a stone sculptor  took a chisel and attempted to “one shot” an entire stone slab?

Honestly it almost feels like these days people just expect AI to be that creative part of the project too and form even the concept of what the game should be. The problem is, there is no passion then and you lack direction. The project is simply going to come out lackluster and problematic as would any other hobby or skill.

the work that you put in is the work you get out of AI
